# When Do Annex III High-Risk AI Obligations Apply Under the EU AI Act?

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act originally set 2 August 2026 as the application date for Annex III high-risk AI system obligations ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence), [Art. 113 AI Act](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113)) (high confidence). However, following the "AI Omnibus" simplification package agreed by the Council and Parliament and entered into force on 27 July 2026, this deadline has been pushed back to **2 December 2027** ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [EU AI Act Omnibus enters into force](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)) (high confidence). Many industry commentaries still cite 2 August 2026, apparently not reflecting this amendment, creating a notable discrepancy in currently circulating guidance ([Responsible AI Labs](https://responsibleailabs.ai/knowledge-hub/articles/eu-ai-act-august-2026-compliance)) (low confidence).

## Key Findings

### Original Timeline (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, June 2024)
As originally adopted, the AI Act provided for full applicability 24 months after entry into force, but specifically delayed Annex III high-risk system obligations to 36 months after entry into force—2 August 2026 ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence), [Implementation Timeline](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline), [Goodwin Law](https://www.goodwinlaw.com/en/insights/publications/2024/10/insights-technology-aiml-eu-ai-act-implementation-timeline)) (high confidence). Article 113 specified that Chapter III, Sections 1-3 (covering high-risk rules, including Annex III) would apply from this date, while Chapters I and II took effect earlier, from 2 February 2025 (medium confidence, [Art. 113 AI Act](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113)). Under the original Article 111(2), the Regulation applied to operators of high-risk systems placed on the market before 2 August 2026 only if those systems underwent significant design changes thereafter (medium confidence, [AI Act Service Desk Article 111](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-111)).

### The AI Omnibus Amendment
The European Commission proposed, via a "Digital/AI Omnibus" package, to delay Annex III obligations by up to 16 months, conditioning the start date on Commission confirmation that necessary standards and compliance tools were available (medium confidence, [Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)). The Council and Parliament reached political agreement on this package on 7 May 2026 (high confidence, [Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)). The legislative proposal was adopted on 19 November 2025 and entered into force on 27 July 2026 (medium confidence, [Shaping Europe's Digital Future](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai)).

### Current Applicable Date: 2 December 2027
Multiple EU official sources now confirm that, following the Omnibus amendment, Annex III high-risk obligations apply from **2 December 2027** (high confidence, [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [AI Act Service Desk Timeline](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/timeline/timeline-implementation-eu-ai-act)). By contrast, Annex I high-risk obligations (embedded in regulated products) remain set to apply from 2 August 2028 (high confidence, same sources). The consolidated EUR-Lex text (version dated 27.07.2026) now references "the date of application of Chapter III referred to in Article 113" rather than fixing 2 August 2026, reflecting this amendment (high confidence, [EUR-Lex consolidated text](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727)). Other obligations remain unaffected: Article 50 transparency rules and certain prohibitions are still stated to apply from 2 August 2026 and 2 December 2026 respectively (high confidence, [AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/faq)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
A significant contradiction exists between EU official guidance (post-Omnibus, citing 2 December 2027) and numerous industry/news sources that continue to describe 2 August 2026 as the operative deadline, apparently without accounting for the amendment (low confidence, [Responsible AI Labs](https://responsibleailabs.ai/knowledge-hub/articles/eu-ai-act-august-2026-compliance), [McKenna Consultants](https://www.mckennaconsultants.com/eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-a-technical-readiness-guide-for-august-2026)). One commentary, published before the Omnibus entered into force, warned that if the amendment wasn't enacted in time, the original 2026 date would apply as a "backstop"—this scenario did not materialize, as the amendment was adopted (low confidence, [LinkedIn/Oliver Patel](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/oliver-patel_when-will-eu-ai-act-high-risk-ai-compliance-activity-7401984085377830912-RglO)). A separate low-confidence source names the amending instrument "Regulation (EU) 2026/1739," while other sources reference "2026/1744," indicating unresolved naming/citation inconsistency ([AnnexOps](https://annexops.com/eu-ai-act-annex-iii-deadline-2027)).

## Knowledge Gaps
It remains unclear whether all transitional provisions (e.g., Article 111) have been fully updated in the consolidated legal text. The precise official citation for the amending regulation is inconsistently reported across sources. It is uncertain whether sources still citing 2 August 2026 reflect genuine ongoing legal dispute or simply outdated material. Further research should clarify interactions between the extended Annex III timeline and other obligations tied to earlier dates, and whether conditional exceptions tied to harmonized standards' availability were retained in the final text.

## Methodology Note
This report was produced by an automated research pipeline: web search, source classification, confidence scores computed from source authority, recency and corroboration, and an automated review against the extracted claims.

contradiction_disclosure.notes: The report explicitly discloses the contradiction between EU official sources (2 December 2027) and industry sources still citing 2 August 2026, the pre-Omnibus 'backstop' uncertainty from the LinkedIn/Oliver Patel source, and the naming discrepancy between 'Regulation (EU) 2026/1739' and '2026/1744', consistent with the Known Contradictions list.

# When Do Annex III High-Risk AI Obligations Apply Under the EU AI Act?

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act originally set 2 August 2026 as the application date for Annex III high-risk AI system obligations ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence), [Art. 113 AI Act](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113)) (high confidence). However, following the "AI Omnibus" simplification package agreed by the Council and Parliament and entered into force on 27 July 2026, this deadline has been pushed back to **2 December 2027** ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [EU AI Act Omnibus enters into force](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)) (high confidence). Many industry commentaries still cite 2 August 2026, apparently not reflecting this amendment, creating a notable discrepancy in currently circulating guidance ([Responsible AI Labs](https://responsibleailabs.ai/knowledge-hub/articles/eu-ai-act-august-2026-compliance)) (low confidence).

## Key Findings

### Original Timeline (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, June 2024)
As originally adopted, the AI Act provided for full applicability 24 months after entry into force, but specifically delayed Annex III high-risk system obligations to 36 months after entry into force—2 August 2026 ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence), [Implementation Timeline](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline), [Goodwin Law](https://www.goodwinlaw.com/en/insights/publications/2024/10/insights-technology-aiml-eu-ai-act-implementation-timeline)) (high confidence). Article 113 specified that Chapter III, Sections 1-3 (covering high-risk rules, including Annex III) would apply from this date, while Chapters I and II took effect earlier, from 2 February 2025 (medium confidence, [Art. 113 AI Act](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113)). Under the original Article 111(2), the Regulation applied to operators of high-risk systems placed on the market before 2 August 2026 only if those systems underwent significant design changes thereafter (medium confidence, [AI Act Service Desk Article 111](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-111)).

### The AI Omnibus Amendment
The European Commission proposed, via a "Digital/AI Omnibus" package, to delay Annex III obligations by up to 16 months, conditioning the start date on Commission confirmation that necessary standards and compliance tools were available (medium confidence, [Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)). The Council and Parliament reached political agreement on this package on 7 May 2026 (high confidence, [Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)). The legislative proposal was adopted on 19 November 2025 and entered into force on 27 July 2026 (medium confidence, [Shaping Europe's Digital Future](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai)).

### Current Applicable Date: 2 December 2027
Multiple EU official sources now confirm that, following the Omnibus amendment, Annex III high-risk obligations apply from **2 December 2027** (high confidence, [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [AI Act Service Desk Timeline](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/timeline/timeline-implementation-eu-ai-act)). By contrast, Annex I high-risk obligations (embedded in regulated products) remain set to apply from 2 August 2028 (high confidence, same sources). The consolidated EUR-Lex text (version dated 27.07.2026) now references "the date of application of Chapter III referred to in Article 113" rather than fixing 2 August 2026, reflecting this amendment (high confidence, [EUR-Lex consolidated text](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727)). Other obligations remain unaffected: Article 50 transparency rules and certain prohibitions are still stated to apply from 2 August 2026 and 2 December 2026 respectively (high confidence, [AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/faq)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
A significant contradiction exists between EU official guidance (post-Omnibus, citing 2 December 2027) and numerous industry/news sources that continue to describe 2 August 2026 as the operative deadline, apparently without accounting for the amendment (low confidence, [Responsible AI Labs](https://responsibleailabs.ai/knowledge-hub/articles/eu-ai-act-august-2026-compliance), [McKenna Consultants](https://www.mckennaconsultants.com/eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-a-technical-readiness-guide-for-august-2026)). One commentary, published before the Omnibus entered into force, warned that if the amendment wasn't enacted in time, the original 2026 date would apply as a "backstop"—this scenario did not materialize, as the amendment was adopted (low confidence, [LinkedIn/Oliver Patel](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/oliver-patel_when-will-eu-ai-act-high-risk-ai-compliance-activity-7401984085377830912-RglO)). A separate low-confidence source names the amending instrument "Regulation (EU) 2026/1739," while other sources reference "2026/1744," indicating unresolved naming/citation inconsistency ([AnnexOps](https://annexops.com/eu-ai-act-annex-iii-deadline-2027)).

## Knowledge Gaps
It remains unclear whether all transitional provisions (e.g., Article 111) have been fully updated in the consolidated legal text. The precise official citation for the amending regulation is inconsistently reported across sources. It is uncertain whether sources still citing 2 August 2026 reflect genuine ongoing legal dispute or simply outdated material. Further research should clarify interactions between the extended Annex III timeline and other obligations tied to earlier dates, and whether conditional exceptions tied to harmonized standards' availability were retained in the final text.

This report was produced by an automated research pipeline: web search, source classification, confidence scores computed from source authority, recency and corroboration, and an automated review against the extracted claims.
